Question: He is the servant of a lady from Edirne. From a young age, she raised him like a son and educated him; he studied sciences, excelled in the art of calligraphy, wrote all scripts without equal, and was a compassionate person. It is agreed that he wrote the rika script better than Yâkût. Throughout the lands of Rum, he was known for his beautiful handwriting; he has poems in Arabic, Persian, and Turkish. He was among the people of knowledge. He was extremely cheerful, delicate, full of enthusiasm, loved pleasure and entertainment, and was a carefree person of taste. Because of his handwriting, the late Sultan Bayezid had given him a stipend. Being extremely carefree and fearless, he despaired and said, 'I do not want to be subject to anyone,' and did not accept the duty. His life ended in misfortune; he died in the Istanbul Darüşşifa (hospital) and his grave is on the Galata side. Which of the following cannot be inferred from the above text about Şevki?

Options:
A) He is among the leading figures of the scribe profession.
B) Although he is a good calligrapher, his rika script is bad.
C) He died in Istanbul and was buried on the Galata side.
D) He is among the scholar poets who composed poetry in three languages.
E) He was raised by a woman from Edirne.
